Bradman grew up in Bowral, Australia, practicing alone with a golf ball and a cricket stump against a water tank. In 1930 he scored 974 runs in a single series. England invented a whole new style of bowling, Bodyline, designed to stop one man. He still averaged over 56. His ended at 99.94. 6,996 runs, 29 centuries, 52 matches, considered by many the greatest achievement in any major sport. In his final innings, he needed four runs to end at exactly 100.
